_comment: v3.66.1237 row-239 battery. The subject is bd-mutate's own validator, so this battery is the tool judging itself -- which is exactly why the mutants target the parts that decide VALIDITY rather than the parts that decide a verdict. M4 is the over-correction: a validator that refuses every .tsx would satisfy every refusal assertion and make all frontend batteries unrunnable. M3's first anchor `if r.returncode != 0:` occurred TWICE -- the shell branch carries the same line -- so it was widened to include the esbuild call above it. A bare condition is not a unique anchor when two branches do the same thing for different languages. FIRST RUN: 4 caught, M5 ESCAPED. esbuild is installed on this host, so nothing drove the branch handling its ABSENCE -- an untested refusal reads as working precisely because the condition it guards never occurs. The same shape v3.66.1230 hit with its empty-population refusal.
